summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Tips Sharing: Clothing Details Edition ## Introduction In this video, we discuss various techniques for handling clothing and model overlap issues in Marvelous Designer, specifically focusing on adjusting pleats and adding detailed folds to costumes. ## Adjusting Fold Details Sometimes, after finishing a costume, we notice that the overall fold appears either too flat or exaggerated. To enhance the fold details, we can make several adjustments: 1. **Select a Costume Version**: Begin by choosing the desired costume version and selecting the interior of the colon layer. 2. **Remove the Face**: This step is important for ensuring the accuracy of the adjustments. 3. **Create a Symmetrical Version**: Press `Ctrl + D` to duplicate the selected layer symmetrically and add it to the interior. ### Importance of Inner Layer Selection The reason for selecting the interior of the colon layer is due to the presence of a pocket version on the outer layer. If the colon is included in the outer layer, the pocket's powder line may penetrate the version, leading to instability. By removing the connection of the inner layer, we can delete any extra inner lines on the colon's version. If not deleted, these lines can cause unnecessary folds when the colon layer is automatically formed, pulling the costume in undesired directions. ## Layer Adjustments With a copy of the inner layer as a foundation, we can increase the number of layers in the design. - Use the **Edit Text Tool** to select and verify that the layer has been successfully deleted. ### Main Color and Pattern Direction The main color should follow the pattern aligned with the kill line, which runs parallel to the arrow. The golden line and vertical line represent the tail. 1. **Increase Tail Lock Rate**: This adjustment widens the outer layer horizontally. 2. **Increase Golden Lock Rate**: This elongates the outer layer, which can introduce folds, particularly noticeable at the seam line. ### Managing Seam Lines At the seam line, especially where pockets are involved, additional attention is needed. - **Using the Ruler Function**: After selecting the ruler tool, a positive collection rate allows you to stretch the grid, whereas a negative collection rate helps to search the grid. Pocket plates are more prone to folds at their divisions. To manage this, create a positive ruler along the edge of the outer plate when aiming for a positive collection rate. ### Particle Distance and Simulation - **Reduce Particle Distance**: This can help simulate more realistic folds. If folds are desired on the clothing plate due to pocket division, set the inner line of the pocket to a ratio of 98 to 99. ## Symmetry and Joint Removal Creating a symmetrical plate directly is not possible if the joint remains. Therefore, it is crucial to remove the joint first to achieve symmetry. ### Fabric Properties and Folds The physical properties of the modified fabric can lead to different fold textures. 1. **Increase Elastic Band and Corner Line Strength**: This will reduce the stretchability of the fabric. 2. **Impact on Folds**: As the inner layer of clothing becomes smaller, the folds will also appear smaller but become easier to produce. The overall fabric texture will deepen. After reducing bending strength, the folds will thin out, appearing sharper and more pronounced. It is important to note that the unfastened order may affect the smoothness of the folds. ## Managing Fold Width and Length To adjust the fold width, it is essential to press and fold effectively. If the fold size is insufficient, further folding is necessary. - **Difficulties with Fold Length**: Reducing fold length to the shoulder may result in a length difference between front and back pieces, leading to minor wrinkles on the front piece. - **Applying Ratios**: You can apply a ratio of 99 to the side to manage wrinkles effectively. This technique is also suitable for sleeve and shirt sides. ## Dynamic Wrinkles Effect For a dynamic wrinkles effect, the **Scenic Comparison Function** can be employed. 1. **Open a Position with Greater Motion**: This allows for the creation of characteristic wrinkles in pants. 2. **Maintaining Wrinkle Texture**: When the position changes to vertical, the Scenic Comparison version retains some of the wrinkles. This method is effective for keeping dynamic wrinkles on a static model. After canceling the Scenic Comparison and simulating, the clothing will gradually revert to its original state. ### Final Notes During the simulation process, you can pause by pressing the control button to maintain a foldable shape effect. These are some straightforward methods to add foldable details to your designs. See you in the next video! ```
